knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Validation is about how dependable the method is against a set standard, rather than training, sterility or approval of a product.
Validation requires consistent success across repeated runs, which one result cannot demonstrate.
The guide lists the moment equipment becomes clean as a first question. The others do not bear on whether the method works.

practicalCriteria: Learner writes answers to the process questions for one named item and identifies which answer needs evidence (pass: all questions answered, one evidence need named).
Learner labels a written example as routine check, verification or validation and gives a reason (pass: correct label with reason).
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Written process-question sheet for one item
stopWorkCriteria: The learner is asked to certify a method as validated without evidence.
A residue or chemical hazard appears that the cleaning method was not designed to handle.
